methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: explores energy efficiency using Specific energy consumption (SEC) model in Kerala’s seafood processing industry

paper_type.evidence_quote: descriptive statistics for monthly production, energy consumption, and energy cost-related parameters in seafood processing units over a period of one year

level_3b.evidence_quote: Energy is an indispensable resource in the seafood processing industry

stage1.notes: SEC (kWh/MT) is central EnPI; also multiple regression + ARIMA. Pooled multi-plant Kerala seafood survey; single applied case. Seafood processing outside continuous-process list; level_3b=false.

multi_site.evidence_quote: Thirty percent of seafood companies under the production capacity of <25 MT/day responded to the structured questionnaire

country_region.evidence_quote: Kerala, a major maritime state in India

type_of_organisation.evidence_quote: energy-intensive procedures including freezing, canning, and drying

evidence_quote: average Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) of 159.2 kWh/MT
Multiple regression analysis (Fumo and Biswas, 2015) were performed
The ARIMA model was employed to analyse and forecast the time series data
